title: VPC lifecycle operator + TF stub playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This draft describes a proposed VPC Lifecycle Operator pattern (Kubernetes controller + TF module stubs) to automate customer VPC activation, upgrades, and graceful rollback for Private deployments (VPC / on-prem). It focuses on operational predictability, small blast radius, and minimal customer-side TF changes.

Scope and goals:
- Automate tenant VPC bootstrapping (subnets, routing, peering, peering ACLs, KMS bindings) using a controller-driven flow that invokes validated Terraform module versions.
- Provide a clear upgrade path for provider module versions and kernel/networking patches with automated canaries and staged rollouts.
- Support air-gapped / on-prem variations with operator+manifest deployment instead of remote plan/apply.
- Minimize required manual steps in customer runbooks; provide an activation checklist and rollback recipe.

High-level operator design (concept):
1) Tenant CRD: TenantVPCRequest {desiredModuleVersion, vpcCidr, environmentTag, egressMode, kmsKeyRef, upgradePolicy}. Operator watches CRs and drives a strategy: plan -> validate -> apply (or create manifest for air-gapped installs).
2) Execution engine: controller delegates to a sandboxed TF runner (containerized), using module artifacts from an internal module registry (signed).
3) Safety gates: preflight checks (IP conflicts, route table verification), dry-run diffs uploaded to artifact store; automatic pause on drift/conflict.
4) Rollout primitives: canary ratio, parallelism cap, automated fallback to last known-good module (tracked in state metadata).

Reference architecture variants (short):
- Cloud-managed tenant VPC (preferred): controller runs in Redwood control plane; executes remote Terraform apply against customer-managed cloud account via short-lived credentials.
- Customer-hosted operator (air-gap/regulated): operator runs in customer cluster; Redwood builds signed plan bundles (TF + vars + validation scripts) delivered over secure channel; customer ops runs bundle with local executor.
- Hybrid: initial bootstrap via customer-hosted operator, ongoing upgrades via control plane if connectivity allowed.

Terraform module stubs (notes for implementation):
- Module: redwood-vpc-core
  inputs (recommended): vpc_cidr, public_subnets[], private_subnets[], azs[], tags, dns_zone_id?, enable_nat
  outputs: vpc_id, subnet_ids, route_table_ids, main_route_table
- Module: redwood-vpc-egress
  inputs: vpc_id, egress_mode (internet/nat/egress-proxy), proxy_config_ref, firewall_policy_id
  outputs: egress_nat_ips, proxy_endpoint
- Module: redwood-kms-bindings
  inputs: kms_key_alias, tenant_id, allowed_principals[]
  outputs: key_arn, policy_snapshot
Implementation notes: modules must emit a signature manifest (sha256) for operator verification. Keep state backend configurable (remote S3/backblaze or local backend for airgap).

Activation checklist (operator-driven steps):
- [ ] Validate requested CIDR vs known allocations (automatic)
- [ ] Confirm peering permissions and routing policy (manual for customer-hosted)
- [ ] Create ephemeral credentials for TF executor
- [ ] Run dry-run and capture plan artifact
- [ ] Run minimal canary (single subnet + route table)
- [ ] Validate connectivity (controlplane -> tenant API endpoints)
- [ ] Promote to full apply or create airgap bundle for customer execution

Upgrade and rollback playbook (short):
- On module release, publish signed module + migration notes.
- Operator picks modules tagged with semver and upgradePolicy from CRD: immediate|canary|scheduled.
- Canary: apply to a single tenant (or single AZ) and run validation probes (latency, route correctness, KV cache behavior for serving runtime).
- If probe failure -> auto-rollback: operator reverts Terraform state by applying previous module version using recorded tfstate snapshot. Notify owning oncall.

Air-gap specifics and constraints:
- No outbound connectivity: operator must accept signed plan bundles. Provide a verify.sh script that runs preflight checks locally and verifies signature and plan checksum.
- State handling: prefer customer-managed local backend (encrypted) with optional snapshots stored on removable media.
- Upgrade cadence: longer freeze windows, require manual approvals in CRD status.

Ops playbook excerpts (runbook steps):
- Troubleshooting stuck plan: check controller logs (/var/log/rdw-vpc-operator), check TF runner container exit code, inspect plan artifact under /artifacts/plans/{tenant}.
- Fixing IP overlap: operator marks CR as error and suggests next free CIDR from allocation pool; operator can propose ARP-free ranges via API.
- Emergency rollback: patch TenantVPCRequest.upgradePolicy=rollback + previousModuleVersion and trigger operator reconcile.

Open questions and todo (short):
- Module signing: integrate with KMS/HSM for key rotation and cross-account verification.
- State sanity: do we store a central tfstate snapshot in Redwood for faster rollback, or require customer-managed state? (Tradeoff: control vs compliance)
- Validation harness: define a small set of infra probes that mimic serving runtime traffic (model RPC, small inference) for canary validation.

Related artifacts and links:
- GH draft PR for operator scaffolding: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/789
- Work item: JIRA PD-4321 (VPC lifecycle operator spec)
- Design notes confluence: confluence:VPC-Lifecycle-Notes-2024

Next steps (actionable):
1) Ship TF module skeletons in infra repo (owner: Liam) — prototype redwood-vpc-core & redwood-vpc-egress by 2024-12-20.
2) PoC operator controller to produce plan artifacts and run a local TF runner (owner: Marisol) — PoC by 2025-01-10.
3) Define canary validation harness and add to Optimize testbed (owner: Devon) — experiments Q1 2025.
4) Security review for module signing and short-lived credential model (owner: Security)

Notes to self: keep airgap bundle minimal (no secrets included), include a README and verify.sh, and ensure all modules emit machine-readable migration hints.

-- end of draft --
